brief: Today's posts centered on Gemini Neon and Antigravity, with several builders sharing launches and tooling tips. The most notable beyond that was a pair of separate Riemann proofs, one from AI and one from a human, announced the same day.

themes.label: Gemini Neon launch
themes.summary: Builders shared Gemini Neon as a fresh release, with Josh Woodward saying it was shipped to prod after a post from @UFO2002616.

themes.label: Antigravity remote control
themes.summary: Peter Yang shared a tip for using Antigravity threads remotely on mobile, saying its remote control works better than Claude's by default.

themes.label: AI Riemann proofs
themes.summary: Amjad Masad and Aditya Agarwal pointed to two Riemann proofs, one from AI and one from a human, released at the same time.

builders.name: Josh Woodward
builders.summary: Announced that Gemini Neon was shipped to prod after a Friday session, with a tip to long-click the model picker on the web. Also thanked @UFO2002616 for the inspiration.

builders.name: Guillermo Rauch
builders.summary: Described the eve personal shopper agent and its new infrastructure, and recommended trying the template. Also noted that ISO 42001:2023 certification now covers Vercel's AI infra.

builders.name: Aaron Levie
builders.summary: Argued that models now solve problems that agents cannot be told how to solve, and expects this to affect finance, legal, life sciences and cyber. Also posted a short note about a big day in math.

builders.name: Latent Space
builders.summary: Published a podcast episode with Cristina Cordova, COO of Linear, on scaling Linear's go-to-market to $100M ARR and on how AI changes issue tracking.

builders.name: Zara Zhang
builders.summary: Advised against sending clients Claude Artifacts or ChatGPT sites, and said that if you curate you should create.

builders.name: Swyx
builders.summary: Asked whether Cursor's origin product has actions or CI/CD yet, and noted that LangChain is rebuilding content, context and software factory tooling after its founder left dbt.

builders.name: Peter Yang
builders.summary: Shared a tip for using Antigravity threads remotely on mobile and said its remote control beats Claude's. Also posted a light note about a Jensen Huang story and a game download.

builders.name: Madhu Guru
builders.summary: Asked for AI people to meet in Chennai at the end of November, noting he now builds AI products at Meta after leading product for Gemini, Veo and Nano Banana at Google.

builders.name: Thibault Sottiaux
builders.summary: Announced an upgraded desktop app that is faster and simpler, and welcomed Akshay with a first tweet. Also joked that an internal experience became too fun.

builders.name: Amjad Masad
builders.summary: Commented on two Riemann proofs, one from AI and one human, and wondered how they will differ in elegance. Also asked whether it is a bear market.

builders.name: Garry Tan
builders.summary: Argued against an asset seizure tax and said California should encourage new startups and spend wisely.

builders.name: Thariq
builders.summary: Described a sports anime game built around elemental bending and said he is now more against handoff. Otherwise mostly personal or playful posts.

builders.name: Dan Shipper
builders.summary: Posted a single short quote about the science of something far greater. Otherwise minor.

builders.name: Aditya Agarwal
builders.summary: Pointed to work on Riemann and a pancreatic cancer pill, and promoted a Nov 25 event in India featuring unit21 and zumutor founders.

builders.name: Matt Turck
builders.summary: Shared a humorous story about automated agentic emailing failing to get a meeting at Slush. Otherwise personal.

builders.name: Nan Yu
builders.summary: Mentioned performance and quality-of-life improvements for frequently used actions. Otherwise minor.
